About Meeta

A background in special education. A calm, attentive way of working with people.

Her story

Dr. Meeta Bali began her career at B.M. Institute of Mental Health in Ahmedabad. Working with children and families brought her close to questions that continue to shape her practice: how a person learns, communicates and experiences the world.

She went on to work in schools in Mumbai, Gurgaon and Kanpur and served as principal of Samarpan, run by SOPAN (Society of Parents of Children with Autistic Disorders). Alongside her work, she continued her studies in special education, completing a postgraduate diploma and a B.Ed., followed by an M.Ed. and Ph.D. at SNDT Women’s University.

For her master’s project, Meeta studied visual strategies for communication in children with autism. Her doctoral research examined HANDLE — Holistic Approach to NeuroDevelopment and Learning Efficiency — and sensory integration interventions. Together, this work reflects her longstanding interest in learning and individual development.

Her later training brought craniosacral therapy, constellation work, Breathwork & Rebirthing and NLP coaching into her practice. Today, she works with clients in Mumbai and internationally, with the choice of approach and session format discussed individually.

She is also an International Teacher in Training in Biodynamic Craniosacral Therapy and welcomes people interested in learning with her.

In Meeta’s words

Presence, patience and deep listening

“My journey has always been connected with understanding the human being: body, mind, emotions and the deeper patterns that shape our lives.”

Working with children and families taught me to pay attention to each person’s way of communicating and experiencing the world. That remains central to my practice.

I value presence, compassion and deep listening. I see my role as accompanying a person, with respect for their experience and their own pace. I aim to offer a calm setting in which a person can feel heard without being rushed.

Professional training

  • Rhythmic Movement Training — Rhythmic Movement Training International (RMTi).

Research & publications

HANDLE & sensory integration

Meeta’s 2012 Ph.D. explored interventions in relation to perceptual, cognitive and behavioural skills in children with autism.

View the doctoral research record

Effectiveness of HANDLE and SI intervention techniques on Perceptual cognitive and behavioral skills of children with ASD.
SNDT Women’s University · 2012.

HANDLE stands for Holistic Approach to NeuroDevelopment and Learning Efficiency. SI refers to sensory integration; ASD refers to autism spectrum disorder.

View the university catalogue ↗

Visual strategies for communication

For her master’s project, Meeta conducted a study on communication supports for children with autism, including objects, pictures, symbols and manual signs.

View the published study

Effect of Visual Strategies on Development of Communication Skills in Children with Autism.
Rubina Lal and Meeta Bali · Asia Pacific Disability Rehabilitation Journal, 18(2), 2007.

The study involved 30 children. Communication scores improved within the visual-strategies group; the difference in post-intervention scores between that group and the comparison group was not statistically significant.

Read the original paper ↗
